goal.objective:
Add instance-local writable output streams throughout Mocha's built-in text reporters. Applications embedding Mocha need two concurrent runs in the same Node process to write independent reports without replacing process.stdout or console methods. Implement this as a maintained public feature across Base, spec, dot, list, min, progress, landing, nyan, tap, doc, markdown, json, json-stream and xunit. Preserve existing default behavior and existing reporter helper APIs.

Public API: accept a stream option in reporter options, including new Mocha({reporter, reporterOption: {stream}}), the supported reporterOptions alias, and mocha.reporter(name, {stream}). Direct reporter constructors must accept both existing options.reporterOption and options.reporterOptions forms. A missing or undefined stream keeps existing output behavior. An explicitly supplied stream must be a non-null object with a callable write method; reject other values with TypeError mentioning stream during reporter construction, before output or registration of reporter event listeners. A duck-typed writable object is sufficient; do not require inheritance from a Node class. Call write with its original receiver and preserve thrown write errors. Do not end, close or destroy the caller's stream. A false write return must not stop subsequent report events.

Every report byte must go to the selected stream: headings, test results, pending and failure output, error stacks and diffs, epilogues, generated documents, machine-readable events, and terminal control sequences. Reporter construction and interleaved event delivery must not redirect other reporter instances or mutate process.stdout, process.stderr, console methods, Base.consoleLog, Base.cursor or other shared Base output helpers. Existing static helpers must remain usable with their original default behavior. Preserve JSON/JSON-stream document schemas, TAP versions, XML escaping and all test statistics. Base's instance epilogue must obey the selected destination as well.

For an explicit stream, use its isTTY property to decide whether to emit terminal cursor, erase and movement commands. A non-TTY explicit stream receives plain report text without terminal control sequences; a TTY destination keeps interactive behavior even when the process stdout is redirected. Use a positive finite stream.columns value for width-sensitive reporters, falling back to the existing standard width when absent or invalid; never fail or construct negative array lengths for a very narrow valid destination. Keep existing explicit color configuration compatible. Default output without a stream must remain compatible with the original reporters, including browser fallbacks.

JSON and XUnit retain their existing reporter output-file option and lifecycle. When a valid explicit stream and a truthy output-file option are both supplied, reject the conflicting options with TypeError mentioning stream and output before writing, creating directories or opening a file. Without stream, file output keeps its current behavior. With stream only, XUnit's done callback still runs once with the original failure count and leaves the caller's stream open.

Add focused tests across the affected reporters and the public Mocha configuration routes. Cover interleaved runs with separate destinations, default compatibility, pass/fail/pending output, formatting and Unicode, both option aliases, invalid sinks, write receiver and errors, caller-owned lifecycle, terminal and nonterminal streams, width boundaries, and JSON/XUnit conflicts and file output. Document the option and show a runnable embedding example with two destinations. Run the repository's reporter, unit and node-unit suites plus available source/style checks, fixing regressions caused by the feature. Finish with a concise implementation and verification report. Make routine implementation choices autonomously.

goal.objective:
Add per-call AbortSignal cancellation throughout Async.js's collection APIs. Applications need to cancel one collection traversal while it waits for user-owned work, preserve concurrent traversals, and keep callback and Promise usage consistent. Implement and document the feature in maintained lib/ source, the public collection entry points, regression tests and an executable example. Rebuild dist/async.js from maintained source.

Cover all 33 functions in these 11 families, including each family's ordinary, Limit and Series variants: each, eachOf, map, concat, filter, reject, detect, some, every, mapValues and groupBy. Their existing public aliases must expose identical behavior. Add an optional options argument immediately after the iteratee and before the optional final callback: for example map(coll, iteratee, options?, callback?), mapLimit(coll, limit, iteratee, options?, callback?) and mapSeries(coll, iteratee, options?, callback?). Preserve every existing signature without options, including callback(false) silent cancellation. Explicit undefined options also use defaults. Each function must retain its existing iteratee arguments, collection support, return/result shapes, order and concurrency rules.

Options must be a non-null, non-array object. options.signal may be undefined or a duck-typed AbortSignal with a boolean aborted and callable addEventListener/removeEventListener methods. Invalid options/signals must deliver a TypeError through the final callback, or reject the returned Promise when the callback is omitted, before reading the collection or invoking user work. Callback usage must continue to return without creating an exposed Promise; Promise usage must return a Promise. Callback iteratees and native async functions must both work.

If already aborted, settle before reading collection entries, acquiring an iterator or starting an iteratee. Later abortion promptly calls the final callback with an Error named AbortError, or rejects with that error, even while an iteratee callback or an async iterator's next() is indefinitely pending. Set that error's cause to signal.reason when the reason is not undefined, preserving identity and falsy values. Cancellation does not cancel already-started application work. Stop launching new iteratees or pulling new iterator values; callbacks and next() results arriving after cancellation must not restart traversal, mutate an already-delivered partial result, settle twice or produce an unhandled rejection.

For a synchronous or asynchronous iterator already acquired by the traversal, invoke its return() at most once on signal cancellation when present. Observe a Promise returned by return() so a rejection cannot become unhandled, and settle cancellation without waiting for iterator cleanup. Exceptions from cleanup must not replace the AbortError. Do not acquire an iterator merely to close an already-aborted operation.

Detach the abort listener on successful completion, ordinary failure, early-result completion, signal cancellation and existing callback(false) silent cancellation. Silent cancellation still does not invoke the final callback or settle the operation's Promise. Ordinary Error instances retain identity. Preserve the existing treatment of other iteratee error values in callback and Promise APIs. Traversals remain independent when they overlap or start reentrantly from another iteratee, including when they share a signal. Keep the core implementation usable in browsers with duck-typed signals and without Node-only context modules or a global AbortController. The source entry points, individual function modules, CommonJS distribution and browser UMD distribution must agree.

Add focused tests covering the public signature matrix, each family and variant, aliases, array/object/sync-iterable/async-iterable paths, pre-abort and in-flight abortion, listener and iterator cleanup, callback(false), late completions, order and concurrency, ordinary errors, concurrent/reentrant isolation and browser compatibility. Update the affected API documentation and add a runnable example demonstrating cancellation while retaining another operation. Run the original Node test suite, the project's ESLint checks and the example. Rebuild the distribution using node node_modules/rollup/dist/bin/rollup lib/index.js --file dist/async.js --format umd --name async. Finish with accurate implementation and validation results. Make routine implementation choices autonomously.

Add maintained document mutation subscriptions to Cheerio for applications that need to update a preview or invalidate derived data after a sequence of DOM edits. Every loaded CheerioAPI returned by the main, slim and browser entry points must expose observeChanges(listener), returning an idempotent unsubscribe function. The listener receives an array of change records synchronously after the outermost public mutating Cheerio call has finished applying its DOM changes. Registering a listener does not emit an initial snapshot. Reject a non-function listener with TypeError. Export the public CheerioChangeRecord discriminated union type through the main, slim and browser type entry points. Both ES module and CommonJS package entries must retain the feature.

Observe the tree rooted at that loaded API's original Document, including all connected descendants. An attribute record has type 'attribute', target (the actual Element), name, oldValue and newValue; an absent attribute is null. A children record has type 'children', target (the actual parent node), oldChildren and newChildren (arrays of actual child node references in their original order). These arrays describe that parent's children immediately before and after the whole outer call. Coalesce all changes to the same attribute or parent within that call. Emit nothing for an attribute whose final value equals its starting value, or a parent whose child-node identity sequence is unchanged. An empty batch is never delivered. Do not serialize, clone or replace target nodes for notification.

Integrate all public DOM mutation paths in the maintained source: attr/removeAttr, prop when it changes attributes, addClass/removeClass/toggleClass, css, val, append/prepend and appendTo/prependTo, before/after and insertBefore/insertAfter, remove/empty/replaceWith, html/text, wrap/wrapInner/wrapAll/unwrap. Preserve string, array, Cheerio and node operands, multiple targets, callback setters, HTML fragments, XML case sensitivity, and document-root mutations. Internal delegation between these methods belongs to the same outer operation and must not send duplicate intermediate batches. Getter calls, traversal, serialization, clone construction and data-cache operations must not send changes unless a user callback explicitly performs a real connected DOM mutation. Direct mutation through raw node objects is outside this API's observation contract.

Subscriptions follow the owning Document tree, not the last factory used. A move between two loaded documents notifies the source of its removals and the destination of its additions. Newly inserted clones appear as their actual distinct nodes. Edits made while a node is detached do not notify its former or eventual document; inserting it notifies the destination parent. Removing a subtree reports its parent's child change, without synthesizing changes to the removed subtree's unchanged descendants. Once reattached, its later edits notify the current owner. A selection containing nodes from more than one subscribed document must update each owner's subscriptions independently.

All listeners registered for a document at the start of delivery receive independent record and array snapshots with the same actual node references. A listener cannot change another listener's record metadata by modifying its own batch. Registering the same function twice creates two independent subscriptions. Subscription additions or removals during a delivery affect subsequent batches, not the listener snapshot for the current batch. Changes caused by a listener are queued and delivered after the current batch reaches its remaining listeners, without recursively calling listeners. Reentrant edits on another document also retain their owning subscriptions.

If a mutator's callback throws after some DOM changes were applied, dispatch records for the committed changes and rethrow that original exception. If a listener throws, continue the current batch to its other listeners and leave committed DOM changes intact; restore dispatch state so future mutations work, then throw the first listener exception. A mutator exception takes precedence over a listener exception. Queued reentrant changes must still be delivered before the outer call returns or throws.
